thread:
Sam: Quick follow-up on the reservation-token + deadline-hint experiment. Ran a small cluster test this morning; observed a 3x inflation in p95 for tiny requests when late-joinions occur after a token has already been reserved. Not just batching overhead — looks like headroom accounting isn't reclaimed fast enough. :thinking:
Priya: Oof. Do you have the timeline of events? is it that tokens are sticky until the batch completes?
Sam: Exactly. Flow: request A reserves token -> batch forms -> request B arrives with earlier deadline -> system tries to late-join but can't steal the reserved credit. Result: B either waits for next batch or preempts whole batch (expensive).
Michael: Two quick ideas: 1) make tokens soft-reservations with reclaim window (e.g., 5ms) and allow priority steals, 2) add a tiny size/latency hint on token so admission can reshuffle before kernel launch.
Tara: Soft-reserve + steal sounds promising, but we need a clear safety net so we don't oscillate (steal -> fail -> reassign -> steal...). We should add a backoff counter on a token to avoid repeated churn.
Priya: Also KV-cache concern: if we allow late-joins/steals, we risk invalidating warm KV cache placement assumptions. Any cache-affinity signal needs to be part of the token. Otherwise we pay warmup cost or increase variance.
Sam: Agreed. Proposal: token = {slot_id, soft_expiry_ts, deadline_hint, kv_affinity_tags, steal_count}. Steal allowed only if soft_expiry elapsed OR incoming deadline < current.deadline_hint - delta.
Michael: That delta needs calibration. In practice we saw 8-12ms margin works for 16k context models on A100 sims. Smaller models could use smaller delta. We should make it configurable per model-profile.
Tara: On implementation surface: admission API change: Admit(request, hints) -> returns token handle. Token has Inspect() and TrySteal(new_request_hints). Keep TrySteal lock-free with CAS on steal_count.
Priya: Telemetry: emit token lifecycle events: issued, claimed, stolen, reclaimed, expired, kv-affinity-mismatch. This will help correlate p95 spikes with steals. Add a histogram for steal latency impact.
Sam: Quick config sketch (for runtime config):
```
{ "soft_reserve_ms": 5, "steal_margin_ms": 10, "max_steal_count": 2, "kv_affinity_required": true }
```
Tara: Love it. Edge cases: what about long-running streaming requests that hold token for seconds? Can't soft-reclaim those. We should classify streaming vs one-shot at admission and avoid stealing streaming tokens.
Michael: Right — add classification hint. If streaming=true, token is hard-reserve and only preemptable by explicit operator override or catastrophic fallback.
Priya: Another operational thought: when steals happen frequently we may be in a mis-sized-batcher regime. Suggest an adaptive controller that increases batch slice granularity or temporarily disables stealing when steal_rate > threshold.
Sam: Good idea. Add an adaptive knob that toggles steal aggressiveness and adjusts soft_reserve_ms based on observed steal_rate and p95.
ci-bot: deploy/exp-rt-batcher soft-reserve feature: succeeded in staging (build 2026.3.14-rtb1). Logs in /artifacts/exp-rt-batcher/171/
Sam: Next steps: 1) patch admission API interface (Sam/Tara), 2) add token telemetry (Priya), 3) run two-week canary with steal_margin variations (Michael). I'll open a short RFC PR with the config and API proto tonight.
Priya: I'll wire dashboards: token lifecycle counts, steal_rate, p50/p95 before/after steal, kv-affinity-miss rate.
Tara: I'll prototype lock-free TrySteal sketch and share perf microbench numbers.
Michael: I'll set up canary job and baseline runs. Let's sync in 48h if we have preliminary numbers. :+1:
Sam: Thanks all. If anyone hits an obvious regress then file infra-alert and tag eng-runtime.
